inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares, Q1 FY2027 10-Q EPS note (basic 1,305.330m + 5.734m dilutive RSUs), post 10-for-1 split of 2026-06-11. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. Slightly conservative: the period-end count is a few million lower after 4.9m shares repurchased in the quarter.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: stock-based compensation expense 310.171 + tax withholding payments on vested RSUs 204.976 (financing). KLA publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA figure, so the two lines are summed per the house rule.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. 10-year UST 5.15% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-13) + beta ~1.25 x ERP ~4.4% = cost of equity ~10.6%; debt is ~3% of EV at ~4.8% pre-tax, so WACC ~10.5%, the house USD default. One WACC across all three scenarios: cyclicality, China and customer concentration are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent is already expensed inside EBITDA; operating lease liabilities (269m at 2026-09-30) are excluded from net debt. One treatment, no separate lease path.
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interest of consequence; none charged.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, three scenarios, via the Drivers route. Routed as a US cyclical operating company (dcf-methods routing table row 2); owner-fcf-adaptations read for the charge-risk-once and working-capital-sign rules. FRESH BUILD, no prior valuation. total_debt is the 5,950m face value of senior notes (carrying value 5,723m is reduced by a -166m swap fair-value hedge adjustment, which is not a reduction in what is owed). cash is cash and equivalents 1,531.950 plus marketable securities 3,209.241. KLA is in NET DEBT, so interest income (177m FY2026) is not stripped from last_fcf; the forward flows are built from EBITDA and carry no interest income or expense. FY0 is FY2026 (June 2026) but the balance sheet is one quarter later (2026-09-30): Q1 FY2027 FCF of 1,336m is therefore both in the cash balance and inside year-1 flows, roughly offset by year 1 being discounted a full period when only 7.5 months remain. Working capital is NEGATIVE capture (-30% of the revenue change): receivables + inventory less payables and deferred revenue run ~30% of revenue, and FY2026 absorbed ~1.1bn of receivables and inventory on 1.4bn of revenue growth. Buybacks are funded (2,290m FY2026, 936m in Q1 FY2027) well in excess of SBC, so the flat count is paid for. Mid-cycle normalisation: FY2027 is treated as a cyclical peak year in the base case (guided Q2 revenue 4.7bn, backlog 12.57bn) followed by a digestion year, not capitalised. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print; the stock moved -13% on 2026-11-05 and is volatile.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR (through-cycle), not equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not usable as the growth anchor: book equity was cut to 1.4bn by the FY2022 accelerated repurchase and has rebuilt since, so the 3-year equity CAGR (29.6%) diverges far more than 30% from revenue (9.0%) and EPS (14.9%). Growth is anchored on through-cycle revenue instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less RSU tax withholding; no interest strip, net debt throughout). Owner FCF: FY2021 1,785m, FY2023 3,062m, FY2026 3,252m. The 3-year owner-FCF CAGR (2.0%) is below reported (4.2%) and far below EPS (14.9%): SBC plus withholding rose from 266m to 515m, and FY2026 working capital absorbed over 1bn. FY2023 to FY2026 also spans a full down-and-up cycle.

base.rationale: Year 1 (FY2027): H1 is 8.84bn (Q1 actual 4.136bn + Q2 guide 4.7bn); H2 at ~4.75bn a quarter gives ~18.3bn, +35%. EBITDA margin is before SBC: FY2026 actual 46.9% (GAAP operating income 5,661 + D&A 394 + SBC 310), Q1 FY2027 49.4%. Long-run 47.5% sits above FY2026 on scale but below the current peak. Cash tax: FY2026 paid 13.9% of pre-tax income, Q1 FY2027 ETR 15.1% with Pillar Two UTPR; ramped to 17%. Capex stepped up to 4.7% of revenue in Q1 FY2027 (FY2026 2.8%) and is faded back. Gordon at 10.5%/3% is 13.7x, below the 16x cap, so Gordon binds.

bull.rationale: No digestion year: revenue compounds ~11% a year for a decade from FY2026 to ~38bn. Gordon at 10.5%/3.5% is 14.8x, below the 18x cap.

bear.rationale: H1 FY2027 is largely booked, so year 1 still grows 30%; the downturn is FY2028-FY2029 (-25% peak to trough, between the FY2024 dip of -6.5% and the FY2009 collapse of -40%). Revenue ends at ~18bn, a 2.9% ten-year CAGR from FY2026. Gordon at 10.5%/2.5% is 12.8x, below the 13x cap.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 is a cyclical peak, not a new base. Backlog of 12.57bn and a 4.7bn Q2 guide carry revenue to ~18.3bn (+35%), and FY2028 adds a little more as 2nm, HBM and advanced-packaging ramps finish. Leading-edge customers then digest: revenue falls 10% in FY2029 and China keeps shrinking as a share under export controls. From the trough KLA grows 4-8% a year, slightly ahead of wafer fab equipment because process-control intensity rises with each node and services (23% of revenue, +16%) compound on the installed base. Revenue reaches ~26.8bn in FY2036, a 7% ten-year CAGR. EBITDA margin before SBC peaks at 49.5%, dips to 46.5% in the digestion and settles at 47.5%.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI capex proves durable rather than a bulge. Leading-edge logic, HBM and advanced packaging keep pulling process-control spend ahead of wafer fab equipment, KLA adds to its ~58% process-control share, and there is a pause in FY2029 rather than a contraction. Revenue compounds ~11% a year to ~38bn by FY2036 with EBITDA margin before SBC holding just above 50% as services scale and DRAM-component and tariff cost pressure fades. China stabilises at legacy-node demand and the Affiliates Rule is not reinstated in a harsher form.
scenario_narratives.bear: The fear behind the November 2026 semicap sell-off is right. Hyperscaler and AI capex is cut in calendar 2027, TSMC and the memory makers push out tools, and backlog (which KLA itself says does not indicate revenue timing) is rescheduled or cancelled. In parallel the Affiliates Rule returns and China, 30% of revenue, steps down again. Revenue falls 25% from the FY2027 peak over two years, EBITDA margin before SBC drops to 42.5% on under-absorption and persistent DRAM-component and tariff costs, and the recovery is a slow 3-6%. FY2036 revenue of ~18bn is no higher than the FY2027 peak.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20%, above the 15% default: 30% of revenue sits under one regulator's export-control regime and a single customer (TSMC) is above 10%, while the balance sheet carries no refinancing risk. Base 50%: a peak followed by digestion is how every prior KLA cycle has resolved. Bull 30%, below the 35% default: it needs AI capex to stay elevated AND China to stabilise AND margins to hold above 50%, with no down year in a decade.

valuation_philosophy.summary: KLA is a dominant, very high-margin franchise valued here on what an owner collects through a full cycle, not on peak-year earnings. SBC and RSU tax withholding are charged as cash costs, working capital is charged on growth, and FY2027 is treated as a cyclical peak. The price is compared with that through-cycle value at a 10.5% required return.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cycle timing: the base case puts a 10% revenue decline in FY2029. If AI-driven capex stays elevated longer the base is too low; if the cut comes in FY2028 it is too high.
Discount rate: with the 10-year UST at 5.15% the model uses 10.5%. Each point of WACC moves base value by roughly 12-16%; see the sensitivity grid and required-return table.
Terminal margin: 47.5% EBITDA before SBC is above any full-cycle average KLA has yet reported at smaller scale.
SBC basis: RSU tax withholding (205m in FY2026, 239m in Q1 FY2027 alone) is summed with SBC expense; it scales with the share price and would fall if the stock does.
Export controls on China (30% of FY2026 revenue) and TSMC concentration.
Working-capital capture of -30% is calibrated on FY2025-FY2026; inventory builds may partly unwind in a downturn, which the engine credits symmetrically.
